question: Which of the following describes Type I FGM?

options.A: Cutting away both the clitoris and labia majora
options.B: Partial or total removal of the clitoris
options.C: Creating a seal over the vaginal opening
options.D: Piercing or scraping the labia majora

explanation: Type I focuses on removing part or all of the clitoris. You'll see this classification often in community health nursing! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T3#GNS225_U6_T3_h3)

question: What makes probability sampling special?

options.A: Every member of the population has a known chance of being selected
options.B: The researcher hand-picks individuals who fit a specific profile
options.C: Only patients with severe symptoms are included in the study
options.D: Participants are chosen based on their easy availability to the nurse

explanation: Spot on! Probability sampling uses fairness and random selection, meaning everyone in the group has a fair shot at being chosen. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T14#GNS217_U3_T14_h3)

question: What is the term for an infection that jumps naturally between animals and humans?

options.A: Nosocomial infection
options.B: Iatrogenic infection
options.C: Zoonotic infection
options.D: Opportunistic infection

explanation: Zoonotic infections start in animals (like rabies or Lassa fever) and find a way to cross over and infect human hosts. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T94#GNS214_U1_T94_h2)

question: What actually happens during an in-vitro fertilization (IVF) procedure?

options.A: Sperm are placed directly into the uterus using a small catheter
options.B: Blocked fallopian tubes are surgically tied and opened
options.C: Eggs and sperm are fertilized together in a laboratory dish
options.D: Hormone injections are given to stop natural ovulation

explanation: With IVF, eggs are collected, mixed with sperm in a lab dish to fertilize, and the resulting embryo is placed into the uterus. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T23#GNS312_U1_T23_h6)

question: Which drug name is given by the manufacturer and always starts with a capital letter?

options.A: Official name
options.B: Brand name
options.C: Chemical name
options.D: Generic name

explanation: Brand names (like Panadol) are created by companies for marketing and are always capitalized, unlike generic names. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T2#GNS125_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following symptoms should a nurse instruct a client to report immediately as a red-flag warning?

options.A: Sudden severe pelvic pain or excessive bleeding
options.B: Mild fatigue after completing a normal workday
options.C: Minor bloating before the onset of menses
options.D: Slight breast tenderness during the menstrual cycle

explanation: Sudden severe pain or hemorrhage can indicate acute surgical emergencies like a ruptured cyst, ectopic pregnancy, or severe post-op bleeding. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T7#GNS311_U1_T7_h8)

question: What is the main difference between HIV and AIDS?

options.A: HIV only affects children, while AIDS affects adults.
options.B: AIDS is curable, whereas HIV infection remains lifelong.
options.C: AIDS is the advanced stage of HIV infection marked by severe immune damage.
options.D: HIV is sexually transmitted, while AIDS is contracted through blood only.

explanation: Think of HIV as the virus, and AIDS as the advanced stage when the immune system gets very weak. Keep pushing! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h1)

question: Which of these does NOT normally change the length of an incubation period?

options.A: The way the germs entered your body
options.B: The patient's favorite everyday meal
options.C: The amount of germs you first caught
options.D: The strength of the person's immune system

explanation: What you love to eat doesn't control how fast germs multiply, but the dose, entry route, and your immunity definitely do! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h3)

question: How does the medication hydroxyurea help treat sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: It increases the production of foetal haemoglobin
options.B: It binds directly to iron stores to prevent liver damage
options.C: It destroys white blood cells to prevent chronic inflammation
options.D: It dilates peripheral blood vessels to lower blood pressure

explanation: Hydroxyurea is a fantastic drug for this condition. It tricks the body into making more foetal haemoglobin, which stops haemoglobin S from clumping together and prevents cells from sickling. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h6)

question: A patient diagnosed with a serious illness insists the lab made a mistake and they are completely fine. What defense mechanism is this?

options.A: Regression
options.B: Intellectualization
options.C: Denial
options.D: Sublimation

explanation: Denial is our mind's way of protecting us by refusing to accept a painful or scary truth until we are ready to process it. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T15#GNS123_U3_T15_h6)

question: Why is it important for modern nurses to get comfortable using bedside technology?

options.A: It shapes every shift and helps protect patients from human error
options.B: Patients refuse care unless digital devices are present
options.C: It completely replaces the need to perform physical assessments
options.D: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on computer typing speed

explanation: You got it! Smart tools are part of daily clinical life, and they act as a safety net to catch mistakes before they hurt anyone. [learn more](GNS113_U4_T3#GNS113_U4_T3_h1)

question: Why is keeping the cuticle intact so important for your patient?

options.A: It gives the nail plate its hard texture
options.B: It controls how fast the nail grows daily
options.C: It supplies the blood flow to the nail bed
options.D: It acts as a seal against bacteria and moisture

explanation: You've got this! Think of the cuticle as a natural bodyguard. It seals out water and germs so they don't slip under the skin and cause infection. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h1)

question: What is the main danger of health workers assuming they know what the community needs best?

options.A: It leads to interventions that the community rejects or ignores
options.B: It causes the government to spend too much money on drugs
options.C: It forces local leaders to step down from their positions
options.D: It immediately stops all outbreaks of infectious diseases

explanation: Ignoring local input results in programs that do not fit the people's actual lifestyle or priorities, leading to failure. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h2)

question: Where are the developing egg follicles primarily housed within the ovary?

options.A: The outer cortex
options.B: The fallopian infundibulum
options.C: The broad ligament
options.D: The inner medulla

explanation: The outer layer, or cortex, contains the ovarian follicles in various stages of development. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T2#GNS121_U5_T2_h5)

question: Which environmental factor easily ruins medications that are sensitive to light?

options.A: Direct light exposure
options.B: Moderate air pressure
options.C: Constant cold drafts
options.D: Low room humidity

explanation: Sunlight and bright lights trigger chemical reactions that break down sensitive drugs. That's why many bottles are amber-colored! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T4#GNS125_U4_T4_h2)

question: Why do many expectorant drugs need to be taken several times a day?

options.A: They require constant physical stomach irritation to keep working
options.B: They have a short half-life and are quickly processed by the body
options.C: They build up toxic levels in the liver if taken only once a week
options.D: They lose their chemical stability if left sitting in the stomach long

explanation: That's right! The body processes and clears them out pretty fast, so frequent doses keep the medicine working steadily. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T3#GNS223_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main result you look for in a qualitative thematic analysis?

options.A: A laboratory value chart for patient diagnostics
options.B: A bar graph showing demographic frequency counts
options.C: Overarching themes that capture the meaning of the data
options.D: A precise statistical correlation coefficient

explanation: You're doing great! Thematic analysis groups all the interview notes into big, meaningful themes that tell the core story of the research. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is early contraceptive counseling crucial immediately following abortion treatment?

options.A: Because hormonal contraceptives immediately cure any underlying uterine infections
options.B: Because ovulation can return as early as two weeks after an abortion
options.C: Because federal law mandates contraceptive use before hospital discharge
options.D: Because patients lose their fertility permanently if they wait one month

explanation: That's right! A woman can get pregnant again very quickly, even before her first normal period returns, making immediate counseling essential. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h4)

question: Which monitoring tool gives the absolute proof that bacterial spores have been killed?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape
options.B: Biological indicators
options.C: Digital pressure gauges
options.D: External pack labels

explanation: Biological indicators use real, highly resistant harmless spores to test if the autoclave truly destroyed all living microorganisms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: Where is the third ventricle located?

options.A: Within the central canal of the lumbar spinal cord
options.B: Directly beneath the outer surface of the occipital lobe
options.C: Inside the core tissue of the cerebellum
options.D: Between the left and right halves of the thalamus

explanation: You're doing great! The third ventricle sits right in the middle, snuggled between the left and right sides of the thalamus. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T9#GNS211_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which of the following is an example of a long-acting reversible contraceptive (LARC) method?

options.A: Combined oral contraceptive pills
options.B: Subdermal contraceptive implants
options.C: Male latex barrier condoms
options.D: Spermicidal foaming vaginal tablets

explanation: Exactly! Implants and IUDs offer long-term protection against pregnancy, but can be easily removed whenever the client is ready. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h3)

question: Why is there fluid between the thin membranes that wrap around our organs?

options.A: To transmit nerve signals to the brain
options.B: To digest food particles in the stomach
options.C: To carry oxygen through the bloodstream
options.D: To reduce friction during organ movement

explanation: Imagine two sliding doors with oil between them. This fluid lubricates the membranes so your heart and lungs can glide smoothly without rubbing raw! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T3#GNS111_U1_T3_h5)

question: What happens to systemic blood pressure when arterioles undergo widespread vasoconstriction?

options.A: Blood pressure drops because the vessel walls become too stretched
options.B: Blood pressure remains unchanged because cardiac output compensates completely
options.C: Blood pressure drops because blood flow through the vessels speeds up
options.D: Blood pressure increases because vascular resistance rises

explanation: Constricting arterioles narrows their lumen, which increases resistance and raises the overall pressure within the arterial system. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which modern workplace design gives workers dual lines of authority where they report to two different managers?

options.A: Simple structure
options.B: Divisional structure
options.C: Matrix structure
options.D: Functional structure

explanation: In a matrix structure, you might report to both your regular department head and a special project manager. It's like having two bosses! [learn more](GST321_U1_T10#GST321_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which household item is a very common fall hazard for an elderly home care patient?

options.A: Bright overhead lighting in the main hallway
options.B: Loose scatter rugs on polished wooden floors
options.C: Sturdy wooden handrails installed along a staircase
options.D: A heavy armchair placed firmly against a corner wall

explanation: Spot on! Those pretty little scatter rugs love to slide underfoot or catch walking aids like canes. Removing them is an easy win for home safety. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T6#GNS324_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why must petroleum jelly and open flames be strictly avoided around active oxygen delivery equipment?

options.A: Grease stops the oxygen machine from making a buzzing sound
options.B: Oxygen strongly supports and quickens combustion and fire
options.C: Petroleum products block the tiny holes in the nasal cannula
options.D: Flames cause the oxygen tank to instantly fill with water

explanation: Oxygen makes fires burn much hotter and faster, so any spark or flame near an oxygen source creates an extreme fire hazard. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why do doctors use a combination of different chemotherapy drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To completely eliminate all side effects
options.B: To target only upper-body lymph nodes
options.C: To finish the entire treatment in a single afternoon
options.D: To attack cancer cells through different angles and prevent drug resistance

explanation: Using a combo team of drugs hits the cancer from multiple directions, making it much harder for the sneaky cancer cells to find a way to resist. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T9#GNS311_U2_T9_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of denial when a patient first gets bad news?

options.A: Manipulating family members into giving attention
options.B: Proving that the doctors made a mistake
options.C: Acting as a psychological buffer against overwhelming shock
options.D: Speeding up the body's physical healing

explanation: Denial is actually a soft cushion for the mind, protecting the patient from absorbing too much heavy pain all at once. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which principle ensures that vulnerable and quiet voices are heard during community health projects?

options.A: Equity
options.B: Profit
options.C: Isolation
options.D: Speed

explanation: Equity makes sure that everyone, especially the poor and marginalized, gets a fair chance to participate and benefit. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T1#GNS124_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is it important to check the discussion section for study limitations?

options.A: It replaces the need to read the results section
options.B: It shows whether the authors are honest about what their study could not prove
options.C: It tells the reader how much money the research project cost
options.D: It provides a list of spelling corrections for the final publication

explanation: Acknowledging limitations helps readers understand where the study might be weak or where results cannot be generalized. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why must clinic staff record refrigerator temperatures at least twice every single day?

options.A: To calculate the exact electricity bill for the vaccine unit
options.B: To catch and correct temperature excursions before vaccines spoil
options.C: To make sure the electric fan spins at maximum speed
options.D: To fulfill government paperwork requirements with no real benefit

explanation: Routine checks allow nurses to spot equipment failures early and move vaccines to safety before they are ruined. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h4)

question: How do kilocalories (kcal) relate to kilojoules (kJ) on food packages?

options.A: Kilocalories and kilojoules are completely unrelated units
options.B: Kilojoules measure only liquid volume instead of energy
options.C: One kilojoule equals exactly 100 kilocalories
options.D: One kilocalorie equals about 4.184 kilojoules

explanation: Different countries use different units for energy. Just remember that 1 kcal is roughly equal to 4.184 kJ. You'll see both on nutrition labels! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T007#GNS227_U4_T007_h2)

question: A patient with a broken arm can walk around and is breathing fine. What triage color do they get?

options.A: Red
options.B: Yellow
options.C: Green
options.D: Black

explanation: Spot on! The 'walking wounded' with minor injuries get green tags and can wait safely while critical patients are treated. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why can the Widal test sometimes give misleading results in places where typhoid is common?

options.A: The test only works on viral pathogens
options.B: Past infections can cause false positive reactions
options.C: Antibodies disappear within two hours
options.D: It requires immediate freezing of the blood sample

explanation: Correct! Because many people have had past exposures in endemic areas, lingering antibodies can trick the Widal test into a false positive. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h4)

question: Why is it smart to check back on a patient shortly after giving them a new intravenous drug?

options.A: To ask if they want extra hospital bed sheets
options.B: To remind the patient to pay their hospital treatment bills
options.C: To collect the empty plastic tray and disposable syringe
options.D: To check for immediate adverse reactions or allergic responses

explanation: IV drugs act fast! Popping back in lets you catch sudden allergic reactions or low blood pressure early when you can easily help. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h6)

question: What crucial step must you never forget before pulling out an indwelling catheter?

options.A: Completely deflate the balloon by withdrawing all the sterile water with a syringe
options.B: Apply heat packs to the patient's lower abdomen
options.C: Clamp the catheter for 24 hours to exercise the bladder
options.D: Disconnect the drainage bag and flush the tube with antiseptic solution

explanation: Never skip this! Pulling out a catheter while the balloon is still full will cause severe, painful injury to the patient. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h9)

question: What is a major health risk for homebound clients who experience long-term loneliness and social isolation?

options.A: Rapid increase in bone mineral density
options.B: Improved short-term memory function
options.C: Enhanced cardiovascular endurance
options.D: Weakened immune responses and cognitive decline

explanation: Humans are social creatures! Lack of interaction takes a heavy toll on both body and mind, making it easier to fall sick and harder to stay sharp. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T2#GNS324_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does the term 'contact time' mean when using a disinfectant?

options.A: The number of hours the nurse wears gloves during the shift
options.B: The time the surface must stay wet with the product to kill germs
options.C: The time it takes for the liquid bottle to completely empty
options.D: The time it takes for the skin to dry after a scrub

explanation: Disinfectants do not work instantly; they require a specific duration of continuous wetness to fully eliminate pathogens. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h4)

question: A student nurse tries to jam a few more syringes into a sharps box that is already completely full. What should you do?

options.A: Transfer the excess needles into a regular black polythene bag
options.B: Leave the box alone until the end of the weekly shift
options.C: Help the student push the needles down firmly with gloved fingers
options.D: Stop the student and replace the box with a new, empty one

explanation: Safety first! Never force items into a full sharps box. Seal it up and grab a fresh one right away to keep everyone safe. [learn more](GST114_U6_T11#GST114_U6_T11_h7)

question: As a nurse doing medication reconciliation for a new patient admission, what is the best first step?

options.A: Copying the medication chart from the previous clinic without speaking to the patient
options.B: Asking the patient to bring in all current medication packages and herbal remedies from home
options.C: Waiting until the patient is discharged before checking their pill bottles
options.D: Prescribing a mild vitamin supplement to replace missing prescription drugs

explanation: Seeing the actual bottles, sachets, or herbal mixes prevents missing crucial details that patients might forget to mention verbally. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T9#GNS215_U1_T9_h4)

question: Why do functional ovarian cysts usually form during the reproductive years?

options.A: Because the uterus stops producing enough estrogen during pregnancy
options.B: Because of normal monthly hormonal changes and ovulation cycles
options.C: Due to bacterial infections traveling up from the vagina
options.D: As a direct result of eating high-fat foods and lack of exercise

explanation: You've got this! Functional cysts are simply tied to your normal monthly cycle and the hormones that control ovulation. Nothing to stress about! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h1)

question: A patient keeps getting severe bacterial infections. Which lab values should the nurse check first to see how their antibody defenses are doing?

options.A: Serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
options.B: Serum immunoglobulin levels (IgG, IgA, IgM)
options.C: Liver enzymes (ALT and AST)
options.D: Fasting serum cholesterol and lipids

explanation: Immunoglobulins (antibodies) handle our humoral immunity. Checking IgG, IgA, and IgM levels helps us see if an antibody shortage is leaving the patient wide open to infections. [learn more](GST114_U4_T7#GST114_U4_T7_h6)

question: Which baby position is required for a planned home delivery to be considered safe?

options.A: Transverse sideways lie
options.B: Any position the baby chooses
options.C: Breech bottom-first presentation
options.D: Cephalic head-first presentation

explanation: A head-first presentation is essential for a safe vaginal birth, especially outside of a hospital. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is the main goal of nursing care when we want to help a patient improve their adaptation skills?

options.A: To ensure the patient relies permanently on hospital staff
options.B: To eliminate all stress from the patient's external environment
options.C: To replace maladaptive habits with healthy coping skills
options.D: To force the patient to forget all past traumatic events

explanation: We can't wrap our patients in cotton wool or remove all stress. Our goal is to coach them toward flexible, healthy ways to weather life's storms! [learn more](GNS314_U2_T2#GNS314_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the job of intrinsic activity when a drug acts in the body?

options.A: It measures the weight of the active pharmaceutical ingredient.
options.B: It prevents the drug from entering the bloodstream.
options.C: It triggers a biological response after the drug binds.
options.D: It determines how fast the kidneys clear the medicine.

explanation: Once the drug locks onto its receptor, intrinsic activity is the spark that actually makes the cell change its behavior. Great job learning the basics! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is your main responsibility as a nurse when a new clinical policy is introduced?

options.A: To rewrite the entire hospital operating budget
options.B: To discard the policy if it takes too much time
options.C: To report the hospital board to the police
options.D: To integrate the new rules into daily clinical practice

explanation: As professional nurses, we adopt updated guidelines into our everyday care to make sure our practice stays safe and standardized. [learn more](GST319_U4_T8#GST319_U4_T8_h6)

question: A hospital pharmacy keeps cash from drug sales in an open drawer and uses it to buy office snacks, leading to empty shelves. Which part of the DRF system is failing?

options.A: Quantification and forecasting
options.B: Manufacturing of raw chemicals
options.C: Revenue collection and banking
options.D: Patient disease diagnosis

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If cash isn't banked safely and gets spent on snacks, the revolving fund stops revolving, and drugs run out! [learn more](GNS223_U3_T8#GNS223_U3_T8_h3)

question: Why would a mental health clinic use a specialty-specific EHR instead of a standard hospital system?

options.A: To allow patients to perform their own psychiatric evaluations at home
options.B: To bypass state regulations regarding hospital bed capacities
options.C: To access built-in templates for mental status exams and stricter privacy controls
options.D: To avoid buying computers for the nursing and medical staff

explanation: You got it! Different fields need different tools. Psychiatry requires special forms and extra-strict privacy to protect patient dignity. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T3#GNS113_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is a major consequence when clients bypass primary facilities to visit tertiary psychiatric hospitals directly?

options.A: Severe overcrowding and longer waiting times at tertiary centers
options.B: Faster recovery times for clients with mild anxiety
options.C: Better funding and resources for primary health clinics
options.D: Elimination of the need for a referral letter

explanation: When everyone goes straight to the big teaching hospitals for minor issues, those specialist centers get overwhelmed. That's why starting at the local clinic matters! [learn more](GNS314_U4_T4#GNS314_U4_T4_h2)

question: What do we call the step-by-step way a disease develops and causes tissue damage in the body?

options.A: Pathogenesis
options.B: Homeostasis
options.C: Necrosis
options.D: Metaplasia

explanation: Pathogenesis is just the medical story of how a disease starts and progresses step by step in the body. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U2_T3#GST114_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which global organization maintains the International Classification of Diseases (ICD)?

options.A: The American Nurses Association
options.B: The National Institute of Mental Health
options.C: The World Medical Board
options.D: The World Health Organization

explanation: The World Health Organization (WHO) publishes the ICD to track health trends and standardize medical diagnoses worldwide. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h4)

question: How does a hemorrhagic stroke cause damage to the brain?

options.A: By causing bleeding that increases pressure and compresses brain cells
options.B: By causing a permanent lack of glucose without altering pressure
options.C: By replacing normal neurons with fibrous scar tissue over time
options.D: By triggering widespread bacterial growth in the ventricles

explanation: Spot on! When a blood vessel bursts inside the skull, the pooling blood builds up pressure and squeezes the surrounding delicate brain tissue. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T12#GNS222_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which everyday habit causes a person to swallow extra air?

options.A: Sleeping on the left side
options.B: Chewing gum
options.C: Eating green leafy vegetables
options.D: Drinking plain water slowly

explanation: Chewing gum makes you swallow air without realizing it, which adds to the gas buildup in your tummy. Good to know for patient teaching! [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h3)

question: What makes a management audit unique compared to a financial audit?

options.A: Restricted to checking mathematical errors in ledgers
options.B: Forward-looking and focused on operational efficiency
options.C: Performed exclusively by external bank examiners
options.D: Conducts only legal trials for corrupt employees

explanation: You can think of financial audits as looking in the rearview mirror at past money, while management audits look forward to make daily hospital operations run better! [learn more](GST321_U9_T4#GST321_U9_T4_h3)

question: Which of these is a must-have rule for running a valid t-test?

options.A: The data must be continuous
options.B: The sample size must be exactly one thousand
options.C: There can be no variability in the data
options.D: All patients must be over sixty

explanation: T-tests need numbers you can measure on a scale (like weight, height, or test scores), rather than just yes/no categories. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h3)

question: A new mother bleeds heavily because a small piece of the placenta was left behind in the uterus. Which of the 4 Ts does this fall under?

options.A: Thrombin
options.B: Tone
options.C: Trauma
options.D: Tissue

question: A surgeon asks for a forceps to securely hold tough skin edges during wound closure. Which instrument should you hand over?

options.A: Smooth vascular forceps
options.B: Fine Metzenbaum scissors
options.C: A small curved hemostat
options.D: Toothed dissecting forceps

explanation: Toothed forceps grip tough structures like skin firmly without slipping, making them ideal for closing surface wounds. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is the main reason for scheduling follow-up visits after dietary counselling?

options.A: Punishing patients who failed to follow their meal plan
options.B: Re-assessing baseline anthropometric data from scratch every week
options.C: Charging additional consultation fees for hospital revenue
options.D: Monitoring progress, reviewing food logs, and adjusting goals

explanation: Right! Follow-ups let us celebrate wins, talk through struggles, and tweak the plan so it keeps working for the patient. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T004#GNS227_U7_T004_h7)

question: Why do different hospital units need to use consistent terms in patient charts?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience any adverse drug events
options.B: It eliminates the need for nurses to write narrative notes
options.C: It ensures clinical terms and data mean the same thing everywhere
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing electronic health record software

explanation: Consistency means any nurse or doctor reading the notes will understand the findings in the exact same way. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h2)

question: Which group of patients is usually most at risk for catching hospital-acquired infections?

options.A: Athletes with minor muscular sprains
options.B: Children with mild seasonal allergies
options.C: Healthy young adults visiting friends
options.D: Elderly patients receiving immune-suppressing medications

explanation: Correct! Older age plus medications that lower immunity make these patients much more vulnerable to infections. [learn more](GST114_U2_T1#GST114_U2_T1_h5)

question: A woman in early labor has an Hb result of 8.5 g/dL. What category does this fall into?

options.B: Normal pregnancy hemodilution
options.C: Moderate anaemia

question: What is the primary goal of establishing a just culture in a healthcare facility?

question: A patient arrives at the ward after a knife wound to the chest, and you notice absent breath sounds on one side. What condition should you expect the doctor to treat with a chest tube?

question: Which factor is most essential for MBO to succeed?

question: Why is it so crucial to give an antidote as early as possible?

question: Why does the pancreas release bicarbonate into the small intestine?

question: What is the primary reason governments get involved in the food supply?

question: Why is active community surveillance just as important as checking hospital record books?

question: Why is growing different types of crops (crop diversity) on small farms good for community nutrition?

options.C: It completely eliminates the need for agricultural irrigation

question: Which of these is NOT a typical cause of a bulging fontanelle?

question: Why is it important for you as a nurse to understand female reproductive anatomy?

question: You are getting a ventilated, unstable patient ready for a CT scan. What is your most important safety check?

options.B: Ensuring portable oxygen, monitor, and emergency equipment are fully functional
options.C: Removing all patient identification bands to prevent scanning delays
options.D: Notifying the hospital cafeteria that the patient will miss lunch

question: In community health, who do we usually refer to as 'stakeholders'?

options.B: Ministry of finance auditors from another country
options.C: Only foreign donors funding the health center
options.D: Patients who refuse to take prescribed medications

explanation: Stakeholders are simply all the key players—from local leaders and health workers to the residents themselves—who care about or are affected by the community's health. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T8#GNS124_U3_T8_h2)

question: Why do large healthcare institutions maintain formal rules and standard operating procedures?

options.A: To replace the need for professional clinical judgment
options.B: To make sure employees never talk to upper management
options.C: To ensure consistent and fair patient care delivery
options.D: To slow down emergency responses on purpose

explanation: Formal rules create uniformity and fairness, ensuring that operations run predictably across departments. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is an ovarian cyst?

question: What are the core parts of a genuine clinical apology?

options.A: A written legal contract signed by the hospital director
options.B: A medical justification explaining why the patient was at fault
options.C: Empathy, acknowledgment of harm, and sincere regret
options.D: Financial compensation and immediate resignation

question: What should you avoid when designing educational messages for the general public?

options.A: Visual aids and pictures

question: What is the primary role of increased protein intake during the lactation period?

options.A: To provide quick energy during night feedings
options.B: To support tissue repair and milk synthesis
options.C: To maintain hydration and fluid balance
options.D: To prevent the baby from developing infant colic

question: In nursing research, what do we actually mean by 'measurement'?

options.A: Recording vital signs only during morning rounds

options.D: Treating patients based on their personal preferences

explanation: Think of measurement simply as giving a number or a clear label to something we are observing, following a set of rules. You've got this! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T1#GNS217_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is avoiding conflict usually an ineffective long-term strategy in nursing?

options.A: It always results in an immediate physical fight
options.B: It forces the nurse manager to fire the staff
options.C: Hospital management requires everyone to fight daily
options.D: The underlying problem usually remains unresolved and may worsen

explanation: Ignoring conflict sweeps issues under the rug, allowing tension to build up until a bigger crisis occurs. [learn more](GST321_U7_T1#GST321_U7_T1_h6)

question: On a Vaccine Vial Monitor (VVM), what does it mean if the inner square becomes darker than the outer circle?

options.D: The vaccine has been frozen and lost its structural potency

question: Why is helping patients become independent so important in home health care?

options.A: Hospitals forbid patients from making any decisions about their meals
options.B: The nurse is only present for a short visit, leaving the patient to manage most of the time
options.C: Patients at home never require any medical supervision
options.D: Physicians prefer that nurses make all lifestyle choices for clients

explanation: Spot on! Since we only visit for a little while each day, the patient needs the skills to handle their care safely when we're gone. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T5#GNS324_U1_T5_h6)

question: What are the bumpy, distinct sections seen on the mother's side of a delivered placenta called?

options.D: Chorionic villi

question: A patient with heart failure repeatedly misses their diuretic medication. What is this patient most likely to experience?

options.A: Severe fluid overload and breathing difficulties
options.B: Lowered blood pressure to normal limits
options.C: Complete recovery from heart muscle weakness
options.D: Rapid weight loss and extreme dehydration

question: Why must community health nurses pay close attention to the well-being of family caregivers?

question: If you visit a home and suspect a vulnerable client is being abused, what is your primary duty?

question: Which of these means a planned home birth is definitely NOT safe?

question: What common economic challenge often forces families to rely heavily on cheap, refined carbohydrate meals?

options.C: Universal free distribution of processed foods at primary healthcare centres

question: You are caring for a stroke patient. Which of these signs needs your immediate action to stop a life-threatening problem?

question: What is an essential safety action you must take immediately before collecting any urine specimen from a patient?

options.C: Administering a prophylactic dose of broad-spectrum antibiotics

question: When is the best time for a patient to give a sputum sample?

question: Which lifestyle habit helps improve blood vessel health for men dealing with sexual dysfunction?

question: Blood-injection-injury phobias are quite unique. What physical reaction makes them different from other phobias?

question: What does 'pulsatile secretion' mean for hormones?

question: A nurse is teaching mothers about ORS preparation. Instead of just lecturing, she asks a mother to come forward and mix the solution herself. Which learning principle is the nurse using?

question: How can poverty make health education harder to put into practice?

question: Which sign shows mental fatigue in neurasthenia?

question: What happens when stock levels drop below a safe minimum in an electronic inventory system?

question: Why does community health nursing place a strong emphasis on health maintenance?

question: What makes home health nursing quite different from working in a hospital ward?

question: Why must we strictly isolate confirmed patients during a viral hemorrhagic fever outbreak?

question: Which of these is NOT a common bottleneck when trying to control government health spending?

question: Which of these is a key part of our fast-acting, innate immunity?

question: Why is checking the airway always the very first step in emergency care?

question: How should you handle a patient who tells you she uses traditional hot water sitz baths for postpartum healing?

question: What is a major ethical worry when healthcare services are driven mainly by private profit?

question: What three major sciences are combined in nursing informatics?

question: What does the 'M' stand for in the SMART objective framework used in healthcare management?

question: What is the main drawback of using a 24-hour dietary recall to check a patient's nutrition?

question: Why are Environmental Health Officers so important to the primary healthcare team?

question: Why is staff health education an important duty for the community health nurse?

question: How can a nurse tell the difference between a cerebellar intention tremor and a Parkinsonian resting tremor?

question: What is one of the biggest benefits of tele-nursing for patients?

question: How do rude or unsupportive ward staff affect student nurses?

question: What is the main reason nurses send a sample to the lab for a microbial culture?

question: How do assisted living facilities differ from traditional nursing homes?

question: How does regular physical activity benefit a patient with Type 2 diabetes?

question: Who is the primary audience for hospital in-service training sessions?

question: Why does injecting local numbing medicine directly into the middle of an inflamed abscess often not work very well?

question: Why can't a nurse just study a huge, broad clinical topic without narrowing it down first?

question: A nurse wants to check if a patient truly understands their new blood pressure medicine. Which question is best to ask?
